script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. Wednesday — here is your MEME recap. The portfolio closed two point two four percent down on the session.

Redwire Corporation dropped its second quarter results today, posting record revenue, record gross margins, and a record contracted backlog — and the market barely blinked. The stock still finished the session in the green, up zero point eight five percent, quietly defying a broad selloff that hit nearly every other name in this portfolio.

No macro data is available for Wednesday's session. The broad market context remains incomplete at this hour, though the weight of red across this portfolio — seven of nine primary holdings finishing lower — suggests risk-off pressure was a meaningful factor across technology and communication services names in particular.

Redwire Corporation is the top story. The company reported second quarter twenty twenty-six financial results, announcing record revenue, record gross margins, and a record contracted backlog — three simultaneous operational highs in the same quarter. That is not a minor footnote. It is a meaningful sign of operational execution in a sector where many competitors are still chasing profitability. Wall Street analysts had already flagged upside potential: the consensus price target on Redwire implies roughly forty percent upside from current levels, according to data cited Wednesday morning. The combination of a strong earnings beat and an expanding backlog gives analysts a concrete basis for that target rather than speculation. For this portfolio, where Redwire sits at nearly seven percent of total weight, the earnings print provides fundamental support for a position that now has numbers to stand on.

Turning to Applied Optoelectronics, the portfolio's largest position at seven point four three percent of total weight. Applied Optoelectronics was down two point three three percent on the session. No specific news drove the move Wednesday, but the name remains tightly correlated to data center optical demand cycles, and broader technology weakness was a headwind across the sector.

Over at Redwire Corporation, as discussed, the stock was up zero point eight five percent. Record results across revenue, margins, and backlog — the numbers are now on the tape. Watch for analyst notes and price target revisions in the days ahead.

AST SpaceMobile was down two point seven four percent on the session. The stock gave back some of Tuesday's sharp gains after three additional BlueBird satellites successfully reached orbit ahead of the planned beta service launch later this year. CEO Abel Avellan described the launch as steady progress toward a space-based cellular network built for scale. The pullback appears to be consolidation after a strong prior-day surge rather than a fundamental reversal.

Meanwhile, Nebius Group was down two point nine nine percent on the session. The company appointed Lindsey Irvine as Chief Marketing Officer Wednesday, a hire aimed at scaling go-to-market efforts during global expansion. Analysts, however, flagged that Nebius does not currently show the combination of factors typically associated with an earnings beat in its upcoming report. Rising spending and margin pressure are the watchpoints heading into results.

Bloom Energy was up two point seven three percent on the session, making it the second-best performer in the portfolio on Wednesday. The company's artificial intelligence data center backlog grew again in the second quarter, with analysts noting the most durable value sits in service contracts rather than product sales alone. A law firm did issue an investor alert Wednesday, though no specific finding or ruling is attached to that notice at this stage.

TeraWulf finished down four point two nine percent on the session. The company held its second quarter earnings call Wednesday, disclosing a major lease agreement with Anthropic and reporting growing high-performance computing lease revenue at its Lake Mariner campus. Despite strong operational progress and robust liquidity, a non-cash loss tied to warrant valuation weighed on the headline numbers. The Anthropic relationship is the longer-term catalyst to monitor.

Lumentum Holdings was down two point seven three percent on the session. No company-specific news crossed Wednesday. The name trades alongside optical networking demand signals, and the session decline tracks closely with the broader technology sector move.

IREN Limited was down four point eight zero percent on the session. No specific news was available Wednesday. The name is exposed to both Bitcoin mining economics and high-performance computing infrastructure build-out, two themes that remain sensitive to risk sentiment shifts.

Sandisk Corporation was the worst performer in the portfolio on Wednesday, down five point four zero percent on the session. No company-specific news crossed Wednesday. Flash storage names have been volatile on inventory cycle signals, and the magnitude of Wednesday's decline warrants close attention heading into the next trading session.

Three items to watch in the next twenty-four to forty-eight hours. First, Nebius Group earnings — analysts have flagged specific concerns about earnings beat probability, so the actual report will be a critical test for that position. Second, any analyst price target revisions following Redwire Corporation's record quarterly results — a forty percent consensus upside is already on the table. Third, continued BlueBird satellite deployment updates from AST SpaceMobile ahead of the beta service launch window later this year.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch closely for any Nebius Group earnings release and further space sector developments overnight.
